newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice sues nursing home for discrimination.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice sues nursing home for discrimination.

text.p: The Justice Department said Wednesday it had brought the first housing discrimination lawsuit against a nursing home, charging that a facility in Akron, Ohio, refused to rent rooms to blacks.

The department's civil rights division said the lawsuit charged the Lorantffy Care Centre had engaged in an unlawful pattern of discrimination against blacks by falsely telling prospective residents rooms were unavailable.

"All potential residents of nursing homes should be treated fairly and given correct information about housing availability, Acting Assistant Attorney General Isabelle Katz Pinzler said in a statement.

The case stemmed from a Justice Department investigation in which blacks and whites posed as relatives seeking information about the availability of nursing home rooms for elderly family members. Blacks were turned down while whites were told rooms were available, department officials said.

The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Cleveland, seeks an order barring the nursing home, its management and certain employees any further discrimination. It also seeks unspecified damages and civil penalties.
